basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Adam vero cognovit Evam uxorem suam, quae concepit et peperit Cain dicens: Possedi'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Adam vero cognovit Evam uxorem suam, quae concepit et peperit Cain dicens: Possedi hominem per Deum. Hinc jam post delicias paradisi et praevaricationis primae reatum, hujus saeculi ac vitae mortalis gesta narrantur, cum protoplasti, qui immortales fuerant conditi, post acceptam moriendi conditionem mortalium ex se sobolem gignere incipiunt, omnibus in iniquitate conceptis, et in delictis materno ex utero prodeuntibus. Interpretatur autem Caïn possessio, cujus causam vocabuli exposuit genitrix ipsa cum ait: Possedi hominem per Deum. Et hoc dicto, mater nostra jam catholica discretione nos docet, quod ita filium peccato suae praevaricationis obnoxium genuit, ut tamen hoc quod homo natus est, id est, quod anima constans et corpore, effectu divinae creationis ac primae benedictionis munere possideret.
